newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sahaviriya to lodge dumping charge on Kazakh steel.
newsitem.headline: Sahaviriya to lodge dumping charge on Kazakh steel.

text.p: Thailand's Sahaviriya Steel Industries, badly hurt by cheap steel imports during 1996, will soon launch steel dumping complaints against Kazakhstan, the company's top executive said on Tuesday.

SSI managing director Adisak Lowjun told reporters that the company has compiled information about alleged dumping, or exporting below domestic prices, by Kazakhstan for almost a year and will submit the complaint to the Commerce Ministry by February for investigation.
Other countries that are likely to face the same charges include Slovakia, Bulgaria, North Korea and some steel mills in China, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina, he said.

The move came after the industry's successful complaints about cheap steel imports from Russia, Ukraine and Poland, which led to the government's imposition of anti-dumping duties of about 25 percent to 52 percent on hot-rolled steel and structural steel from those countries.
The tariffs were levied from December 27 last year.
"Before we can lodge any charge, we must have solid information and evidence to make the government comfortable enough to investigate it," Adisak said.

Adisak estimated steel imports from Kazakhstan amounted to between 50,000-100,000 tonnes a year. The hot-rolled steel was sold at around $260-270 per tonne here while Sahaviriya Steel's product sold at around $340 per tonne.
According to the World Trade Organisation, Thailand must prove the dumping actually took place and that it has had a negative impact on Thai steel makers before anti-dumping duties can be imposed.
Thailand imported around 1.4-1.5 million tonnes of steel in 1996. According to Adisak, almost 80 percent of that amount came from countries that dumped on markets, mostly Russia and Ukraine.

The cheap imports, coupled with an economic slowdown, have dented Sahaviriya Steel's performance since mid-1995. The company reported a net loss of 189 million baht ($7.56 million) in 1995 which grew to a 1.64 billion baht loss for the first nine months of 1996.
Total 1996 sales amounted to 9.52 billion baht -- far below the company's target of 15 billion baht, Adisak said.
But he said he expects the company's performance to improve this year now that anti-dumping duties are being imposed on cheap hot-rolled steel.
